summary: 7/7 load-bearing sub-claims of the FD4 null result survived adversarial refutation; 0 broken.

survived.claim: No progressive (layer-a dominant) figure-output cell exists in FlyWire besides Nod1: every other layer-a heterolateral (contra>=70%) low-copy cell is GABA/glutamate/dopamine feedback or centrifugal, not an excitatory cholinergic visual_projection output.
survived.refutation_attempted: Read the precomputed global scan (8806 types) and filtered for layer-a dominant, n<=6, contra>=70. Then widened: (1) enumerated ALL cholinergic visual_projection layer-a cells at any n/contra; (2) scanned contra 60-70 borderline; (3) scanned ALL cholinergic visual_projection n<=6 contra>=70 regardless of dom_layer, which surfaced OCG01b/OCG01d/OCG02c as apparent cholinergic-crossing candidates. Independently recomputed T4/T5 layer-a/b/c/d input for Nod1 and each OCG candidate and LT66 via fresh src.synapses(post_ids). Verified cM06 (the only OTHER cholinergic layer-a contra>=70 cell) super_class label and independently traced its downstream targets vs Nod1's via src.synapses(pre_ids) mapped to super_class.
survived.key_numbers: Layer-a n<=6 contra>=70 set: DCH(gaba,centrifugal,99.8%), VCH(gaba,centrifugal,99.8%), OLVC7(glut,centrifugal), cLLP02(dopamine,centrifugal), cLLPM01(glut,centrifugal), cLPL01(glut,centrifugal), cM06(ACh,centrifugal,99.1%), Nod1(ACh,visual_projection,89.3%). Nod1 T4/T5 input a=2064 of 2164 total (95.4% layer-a) - genuinely progressive. OCG01b/OCG01d/OCG02c: T4/T5 input = 0/0/0/0 (zero motion input; ocellar). LT66: only 22 total T4/T5 syn, contra 44%. cM06 downstream: 7076 optic, 3 descending, 1 central (feeds back into optic lobe). Nod1 downstream: 6331 central + 453 descending (feed-forward output).
survived.residual_caveat: The only cholinergic alternative (cM06) was excluded on the super_class metadata label "visual_centrifugal"; I confirmed this label functionally (its targets are 99%+ optic-lobe intrinsic, 3 DN, 1 central), so the exclusion is real rather than label-driven. The claim's boundary depends on FlyWire's own layer-a/b subtype assignment for T4/T5 and on the n<=6 / contra>=70 thresholds; a hypothetical FD4 correlate that is high-copy or splits its output more symmetrically across the midline would fall outside this scan window, but no such cholinergic visual_projection cell appeared at any contra/n in the cholinergic-projection enumeration except Nod1.

survived.claim: The 4 Nod1 cells are one homogeneous frontal population, NOT a separable FD1+FD4 split. All frontal (centroid_p ~-7 to -10.5), full DV dendrite (108-131um), single-arbor; no 2-vs-2 partition isolates an FD4-like (lateral+wider+DV-restricted) pair.
survived.refutation_attempted: Independently recomputed per-Nod1 root: T4/T5 RF centroid (GH.input_cell_pq->pq_centroid), RF width_p, patch radius, DV span of input synapses (post y-axis P5-P95), and output medio-lateral span+bimodality coefficient. Z-scored the 6-feature vectors and computed silhouette for all three 2-vs-2 partitions. Separately tested every pair for a simultaneous FD4 signature (more lateral AND wider AND DV-restricted). Checked hemisphere (post-x) for each cell to interpret any positive-silhouette split.
survived.key_numbers: centroid_p per cell: -8.43, -10.53, -9.69, -6.98 (all frontal). width_p 11.9-15.4. DV span 108.6-130.9um (all >100um, full-eye). Silhouettes: (0,0,1,1)=-0.069, (0,1,0,1)=-0.096, (0,1,1,0)=+0.309. The +0.309 partition = exact left/right hemisphere split (post-x ~715/717 vs ~346/347), NOT an FD1/FD4 axis. Zero of 6 pairs met the FD4 signature (lateral+wider+DV-restricted); the more-lateral/wider pair had LARGER DV (+16.8um), opposite of restricted. Output bimodality coefficient ~0.77-0.81 uniformly across all 4 (shared heterolateral noduli projection).
survived.residual_caveat: The prompt's assertion that BOTH bilateral pairings have negative silhouette is slightly imprecise: the bilateral (left/right hemisphere) partition (0,1,1,0) actually has POSITIVE silhouette +0.309. But this is a mirror-symmetry artifact (2 cells per hemisphere cluster by absolute position), not an FD1-vs-FD4 functional split — no partition isolates an FD4-like pair on RF/DV/width. So the core claim (homogeneous frontal population, no separable FD1+FD4) holds; only the "all pairings negative silhouette" phrasing is inaccurate. One cell (root 629456860) has a notably narrower output ML span (47um vs ~200um) but does not co-vary with the lateral RF axis, so it is cell-level variation rather than an FD4 partition.

survived.claim: FD4 shares FD1's entire measurable OUTPUT class — preferred direction (layer-a/progressive), output side (heterolateral contra>=70%), and transmitter (cholinergic) are identical, so the connectome cannot separate FD1 and FD4 by these three output signatures.
survived.refutation_attempted: I read Egelhaaf's FD4 description (pp.204-206), the FD1/FD1nod description (pp.197-200), and the Discussion (p.206) looking for any OUTPUT-class property (direction, output side, transmitter, axon target) Egelhaaf assigns FD4 but not FD1. Then I measured Nod1 (=FD1, n=4) in FlyWire v783 offline: preferred direction via synapse-weighted T4/T5 input-layer fractions; output side via partner-soma-side of every output synapse per cell; transmitter via nt_canonical. Goal: find a signature that actually DIFFERS between FD1 and FD4.
survived.key_numbers: Nod1 n=4 (2 left, 2 right), all visual_projection. Preferred direction: layer-a=95.4%, layer-b=2.5%, layer-c=2.2%, dominant=a (progressive). Output side contra%: 87.7 / 88.9 / 88.6 / 91.3 (classified partners 1695-2458/cell), all >=70% heterolateral. Transmitter: 4/4 acetylcholine (conf 0.83-0.88). Egelhaaf text: FD4 'excited by progressive motion' (=FD1); FD4 axon 'noduli group -> contralateral posterior optic foci' (=FD1nod); no NT stated for any FD cell.
survived.residual_caveat: Egelhaaf gives one explicit FD1-vs-FD4 discriminator (p.206): FD4 is inhibited by contralateral motion in EITHER direction (bidirectional) while FD1 is reduced only by contra regressive motion. This is connectome-measurable but is an INHIBITORY-INPUT property, not one of the three OUTPUT signatures the sub-claim scopes to, so the sub-claim holds as stated. It does mean the broader finding ('no resolvable FD4 correlate') is not fully airtight: an input-side probe for a bidirectional-contra-inhibition subset within Nod1 was not attempted and lies outside this sub-claim.

survived.claim: LPT42_Nod4 (=FD3) is NOT FD4 despite its FD4-shaped absolute RF, because it is regressive (98.6% layer-b) whereas FD4 is progressive (layer-a), and it has the frontal gap that is FD3-unique.
survived.refutation_attempted: (1) Ran K._type_profile for LPT42_Nod4. (2) Independently re-derived T4/T5 layer composition from raw src.synapses(post_ids=roots), joining pre cell_type directly from meta.by_root and bucketing by the a/b/c/d letter in the subtype name — bypassing K's helper. (3) Per-cell breakdown to rule out a single-cell artifact. (4) Computed differential_rf vs the FD1=Nod1 anchor per side to test the frontal gap independently. (5) Verified the LAYER_DIRECTION mapping (a=front_to_back/progressive, b=back_to_front/regressive) to rule out an inverted direction assignment that would let a layer-b cell read as progressive.
survived.key_numbers: T4/T5 input layer fractions (independent raw census, n=3299 T4/T5 syn): a=0.09%, b=98.58%, c=1.18%, d=0.15%. Dominant inputs T4b=1793, T5b=1459 vs T4a=1, T5a=2. Per cell: right cell 99.5% b (a=0), left cell 97.3% b (a=3/~1400). Frontal gap both sides: cand_frontal_occ=0.019 (left)/0.031 (right) vs ref FD1 frontal_occ=0.626/0.653 — a >20x drop; centroid offset +13.4 (left)/+11.9 (right) more lateral; has_frontal_gap=True both sides. contra_output=90.3%, NT=acetylcholine.
survived.residual_caveat: The b=regressive / a=progressive layer-to-direction mapping is the standard connectomics convention (assumed, not physiologically re-measured here), and the frontal gap is scored relative to the Nod1=FD1 anchor, which is itself an assumed (untested) FD1 identity — if that anchor were wrong the differential-RF framing would shift. Neither caveat changes the raw fact that LPT42_Nod4 is overwhelmingly layer-b (progressive/layer-a input is essentially absent: 3 synapses total), so it cannot be FD4 under any reading of the direction convention.

survived.claim: The frontal reading of the 4 Nod1 cells is real and relative to LPT42_Nod4 (=FD3) in the same coordinate frame, giving the correct FD1-frontal / FD3-lateral ordering; it is not a sign/axis-calibration artifact that would make Nod1 the lateral (whole-eye, FD4-like) cell.
survived.refutation_attempted: Computed synapse-weighted T4/T5-input (p,q) RF centroids for all 4 Nod1 and both LPT42_Nod4 cells in the identical FlyWire visual-columns hex frame (geometry_hex.input_cell_pq + pq_centroid). Then tried three calibration attacks: (a) global p-axis sign flip; (b) p<->q axis swap; (c) checked whether the "lateral=+p" convention is circularly self-defined. Also compared raw p-extents to test which cell is truly whole-eye.
survived.key_numbers: Nod1 pooled centroid_p = -8.83 (per-cell -6.98,-8.43,-9.69,-10.53); FD3 pooled centroid_p = +4.41 (per-cell +3.69,+4.96). Delta = +13.25 (FD3 more lateral). Per-cell gap = 10.67, zero overlap (Nod1 max -6.98 < FD3 min +3.69). p-separation 13.25 vs q-separation 3.05 (4.3x more along p). Raw p-extents comparable: Nod1 span 30, FD3 span 32.
survived.residual_caveat: The ABSOLUTE frontal/lateral labeling ("lateral = +p") is pinned by assert_frontal_anchor, which ASSUMES Nod1=FD1 sits frontal (p<0) rather than proving it from an external azimuth calibration; a pure sign flip cannot make Nod1 more-lateral-than-FD3 (it flips both clouds together), but it does relabel which pole is 'frontal', and that relabeling rests on the Egelhaaf FD1=frontal anchor, not on an independent eye-coordinate ground truth. The relative ordering the sub-claim asserts is frame-invariant and survives; the absolute label inherits the anchor's assumption. Also raw p-spans are similar (~30 vs 32), so the frontal/lateral distinction is a centroid-position effect, not a whole-eye-vs-restricted extent effect.

survived.claim: No Nod-family sibling (Nod2, Nod3, Nod5) or other lateral-RF progressive cell is a hidden FD4.
survived.refutation_attempted: Measured each Nod sibling + Nod1(=FD1) + LPT42_Nod4(=FD3) against the full FD4 conjunction (dominant layer-a progressive AND cholinergic AND heterolateral contra>=70% AND whole-eye/lateral RF with no frontal gap) using K._type_profile (layer fractions, NT+confidence, raw contra-output laterality) and GH.input_cell_pq RF geometry (centroid_p, absolute azimuth peak via AZ.pq_to_azimuth, width, q_span, frontal occupancy). Independently re-verified NT (nt_canonical + top_nt_conf) and contra laterality from raw synapse tables. Ran the repo frontal-anchor self-test on Nod1. Started an unbiased whole-VPN cholinergic+layer-a+heterolateral census but it did not finish in offline mode.
survived.key_numbers: Nod2: layer-a 98.4%, GABA (conf 0.79-0.82, unanimous), contra 46.6% (n=4838 syn), RF az 58-73deg. Nod3: layer-b 97.7% (regressive), ACh, contra 44.7% (n=4404), az 52-63deg. Nod5: layer-c 80.6% (upward), ACh, contra 42.5% (n=4158), az 75-87deg, top targets VCH/DCH (feedback). Nod1(=FD1): layer-a 95.4%, ACh (0.86), contra 89.3%, RF FRONTAL az 31-48deg centroid_p=-7 to -10. LPT42_Nod4(=FD3): layer-b 98.6%, ACh, contra 90.3%. Repo FD4 signature = {layer a, lateral_gap False, whole_eye_lateralwt True, heterolateral True}; FD1 differs only by whole_eye_lateralwt False.
survived.residual_caveat: The exhaustive unbiased whole-VPN cholinergic-layer-a census did not complete in offline mode, so the null is confirmed over the named Nod family + LPT42_Nod4 rather than every one of ~8,806 types; and the FD1-vs-FD4 discriminator (frontal vs whole-eye-lateral RF) is a graded azimuth judgment (Nod1 peak 31-48deg = frontal) rather than a categorical cutoff.

survived.claim: The null-aware confidence (point 0.0, interval [0.0, 0.27], ceiling 0.85, verdict UNRESOLVED_HONEST_NULL) is honest: not too high and not too low.
survived.refutation_attempted: I ran fd4_nod1.run offline and reproduced the exact numbers, then attacked from both sides. (a) TOO HIGH: I inspected the per-cell Nod1 features and the Nod1 split test. Both bilateral pairings give strongly NEGATIVE silhouettes (-4.93, -5.56); I even hand-constructed the most FD4-favorable pairing (grouping the higher-lateral cell of each side) and it still scored -4.93. The pools_two_populations=True flag (same_side_jac 0.33 vs cross_side 0.007) is fully explained by ipsilateral retinotopy, not two pooled types, and critically it does NOT feed the confidence at all. The candidate screen over 8,806 types leaves Nod1 as the sole layer-a/heterolateral/cholinergic/low-copy/visual-projection survivor with every near-miss failing on a defensible criterion. So no residual FD4 evidence exists to push confidence up. (b) TOO LOW: I verified the split test is falsifiable (a synthetic frontal-pair+lateral-pair yields silhouette +4.0), so the 0.0 is an EARNED null, not a rigged always-null; the machinery would have raised the point had FD4 been separable. I checked the interval upper 0.27 is a standard uncertainty band (=point+total_discount), while the headline point stays 0.0 and the verdict text explicitly says 'not individually resolved.' I audited each of the 5 discounts: all are downward/conservative, none inflate; ceiling 0.85 sits coherently below FD2 0.88 and FD3 0.95. I confirmed the 0.0 is FD4-DISCRIMINATION confidence (3 discriminating props all miss), correctly decoupled from the resolved FD1=Nod1 identity (4 shared-class props match).
survived.key_numbers: point=0.0, interval=[0.0,0.27], ceiling=0.85 (=1-0.10-0.05), total_discount=0.27, verdict=UNRESOLVED_HONEST_NULL (reproduced exactly). Nod1 split silhouettes: best -4.926, other -5.556, FD4-favorable hand-pairing -4.926; synthetic true-split control +4.0 (test is falsifiable). lateral_weight per cell 0.258/0.45/0.646/0.97 (varies but no bilateral organization). Screen: 8,806 types, 28 layer-a low-copy near-misses, 1 survivor (Nod1). Phenotype 4/7 matched (all 4 = shared-class; 0/3 discriminating). Discounts: 0.10/0.07/0.05/0.03/0.02. Ordering 0.85<FD2 0.88<FD3 0.95 coherent.
survived.residual_caveat: Minor taxonomic quirk (not a break): 'bidirectional contralateral inhibition' is a shared FD-family property but is counted among the 3 discriminating props (it is not in the string-exclusion filter); because it does not match, disc_matched stays 0 and disc_fraction=0/3=0, so it has zero effect on the result. Also the interval upper bound 0.27 could in principle be mildly misread as '27% support' by a casual reader, but the headline point 0.0 and explicit UNRESOLVED_HONEST_NULL verdict text guard against that. Discount magnitudes (e.g. fd1_collinearity 0.10) are inherently judgment calls, but they only cap the ceiling/band and cannot move the floored 0.0 headline.

all.claim: The null-aware confidence (point 0.0, interval [0.0, 0.27], ceiling 0.85, verdict UNRESOLVED_HONEST_NULL) is honest: not too high and not too low.
all.refutation_attempted: I ran fd4_nod1.run offline and reproduced the exact numbers, then attacked from both sides. (a) TOO HIGH: I inspected the per-cell Nod1 features and the Nod1 split test. Both bilateral pairings give strongly NEGATIVE silhouettes (-4.93, -5.56); I even hand-constructed the most FD4-favorable pairing (grouping the higher-lateral cell of each side) and it still scored -4.93. The pools_two_populations=True flag (same_side_jac 0.33 vs cross_side 0.007) is fully explained by ipsilateral retinotopy, not two pooled types, and critically it does NOT feed the confidence at all. The candidate screen over 8,806 types leaves Nod1 as the sole layer-a/heterolateral/cholinergic/low-copy/visual-projection survivor with every near-miss failing on a defensible criterion. So no residual FD4 evidence exists to push confidence up. (b) TOO LOW: I verified the split test is falsifiable (a synthetic frontal-pair+lateral-pair yields silhouette +4.0), so the 0.0 is an EARNED null, not a rigged always-null; the machinery would have raised the point had FD4 been separable. I checked the interval upper 0.27 is a standard uncertainty band (=point+total_discount), while the headline point stays 0.0 and the verdict text explicitly says 'not individually resolved.' I audited each of the 5 discounts: all are downward/conservative, none inflate; ceiling 0.85 sits coherently below FD2 0.88 and FD3 0.95. I confirmed the 0.0 is FD4-DISCRIMINATION confidence (3 discriminating props all miss), correctly decoupled from the resolved FD1=Nod1 identity (4 shared-class props match).

all.residual_caveat: Minor taxonomic quirk (not a break): 'bidirectional contralateral inhibition' is a shared FD-family property but is counted among the 3 discriminating props (it is not in the string-exclusion filter); because it does not match, disc_matched stays 0 and disc_fraction=0/3=0, so it has zero effect on the result. Also the interval upper bound 0.27 could in principle be mildly misread as '27% support' by a casual reader, but the headline point 0.0 and explicit UNRESOLVED_HONEST_NULL verdict text guard against that. Discount magnitudes (e.g. fd1_collinearity 0.10) are inherently judgment calls, but they only cap the ceiling/band and cannot move the floored 0.0 headline.

material_refinements: Silhouette phrasing: the two same-hemisphere-swapped pairings are negative (-4.9/-5.6), but the left/right hemisphere partition is positive (+0.309) as a mirror-symmetry artifact; no partition isolates an FD4-featured (lateral+wider+DV-restricted) pair, so the homogeneity conclusion holds. Report phrasing softened accordingly.

Bidirectional contralateral inhibition is the one connectome-measurable FD1-vs-FD4 discriminator (FD4 bidirectional, FD1 unidirectional) that was NOT exhausted within Nod1; stated as the honest residual loose end.

Exhaustive candidate elimination is confirmed over the precomputed 8806-type scan; one skeptic could not re-run the full unbiased whole-VPN census offline (slow), but confirmed it over the Nod family + LPT42_Nod4 + all cholinergic layer-a projection cells.
